## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Tacasārajātaka* (Ja 368) is a birth story in the Pali *Jātaka* collection. Set at Jetavana, the discourse was delivered by the Buddha concerning the Perfection of Wisdom (*paññāpāramī*), observing that the Tathāgata was similarly wise and resourceful in past lives [Fausböll 1883]. The narrative recalls an ancient time when Brahmadatta was reigning in Bārāṇasī, opening with the verse beginning *Amittahatthatthagatā ti* [Fausböll 1883]. In the concluding identification (*samodhāna*), the Buddha reveals that the King of Bārāṇasī was Ānanda, the other youths were senior theras (*therānutherā*), and the wise youth (*paṇḍitadārako*) was the Buddha himself in a former birth [Fausböll 1883].
